slides.title: Reversing Harlow's margin decline

paragraphs.text: Margin plan for the board, February 2027
Board of directors, presented by the CEO

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Fix promotions, delivery fees and weak stores now and cut hours last: that clears the covenant and reaches 2.7% by FY2028, and 3.0% with a second promotion wave
Wages are not the main cause: promotions, e-commerce and shrink explain 87% of the margin lost
–	Labor rose only 0.3 percentage points of sales despite a 9.4% wage rise
–	38% of promotional events lost money; e-commerce loses about $10M a year
Management's 8% hours cut loses much of its saving to shrink; FY2028 profit stays near today's
–	Leanest-staffed stores lose 3.1% of sales to shrink, the best-staffed 2.3%
–	Net of shrink and the wage rise, FY2028 operating income stays near $16M
Five moves on the real causes add about $22M a year by FY2028, led by store exits and promotions
–	Promotions back to their FY2023 share add about $6M after lost volume; exits $6.6M
–	Six of the nine leases lapse by 2027, so only three exits need a board vote
With hours cut last, the plan clears the covenant and reaches 2.7% by FY2028; 3.0% needs more promotion cuts
–	Operating income reaches about $38M after $7M of known cost increases
–	Cutting promotions to about 21% of sales reaches 3.0%; the stress case stops at 2.1%

slides.title: Promotions, e-commerce and shrink, not wages, explain 87% of the operating margin Harlow lost since FY2023

paragraphs.text: Promotions, e-commerce and shrink, not wages, explain 87% of the operating margin Harlow lost since FY2023
Operating margin, % of sales, FY2023 to FY2025; each step is the change in that line's share of sales
of the margin decline comes from promotions, e-commerce fulfillment and shrink
▪	Promotional mix: 5 more percentage points of sales sold on promotion, each earning 14 percentage points less
▪	E-commerce fulfillment: grew from 0.4% to 1.2% of sales as online orders nearly tripled
▪	Shrink: up from 2.1% to 2.6% of sales, worst in the leanest-staffed stores
▪	Store labor: only 0.3 percentage points, the smallest cost line that rose
1  Promotional mix = change in share × 14 percentage points lower margin; private label = change in share × 12 percentage points higher. Part of the shrink rise reflects thinner staffing (p. 9)
Sources: Harlow Fresh Markets briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis

paragraphs.text: Net of shrink and the 2027 wage rise, management's labor plan leaves FY2028 operating income near today's, at $16M
Operating income under management's plan, $ millions, FY2025 actual to FY2028 run-rate
2027 minimum-wage rise: 4% on today's $181.9M store labor
management's estimate for 8% fewer store hours
Even on generous assumptions, the cut nets about $8.0M and fixes none of the bigger causes
▪	Shrink responds to hours as in FY2023–25, when hours per $1,000 of sales fell 6.0% and shrink rose 0.5 percentage points
▪	Only fresh waste and receiving errors, 65% of shrink, respond to staffing; theft does not
▪	Customer response to longer checkout waits and stock-outs is not counted, so this is a best case
▪	E-commerce frozen at its FY2025 size, still losing about $10M a year; promotions unchanged
The labor plan targets the smallest cause of the decline and gives back almost half its saving in shrink
1  Prices, volumes and other costs held at FY2025 levels; formulas in the Calculations sheet of the source workbook

paragraphs.text: Private label is a cheaper value signal than deeper promotions; holding today's pace adds about $3.8M by FY2028

▪	Price image: 41% of shoppers now call Harlow more expensive, up from 33% in FY2023, despite deeper promotions
▪	Margin: each share point in private label earns 12 percentage points more, where promotion costs 14
added FY2026–28: 0.75 pp a year, the FY2023–25 pace, × 3 years

slides.title: Next steps

paragraphs.text: Cut the money-losing promotional events and reopen vendor-funding talks; keep depth in ValuMart trade areas
Roll out the $7.99 delivery fee and $100 threshold chain-wide; push for a flat rate at the delivery renewal
Vote on the three early store exits ($7.5M one-time) and give notice on the six leases ending by 2027
Restore receiving and produce rotation in the leanest stores; hold the hours cut until shrink there is at or below 2.4%
Decide on a second promotion wave, bringing promotions to about 21% of sales, if sales near ValuMart hold
Report the five gates to the board every quarter, starting with promotional share against 26.0%
